metadata.file_name: J Res Sci Teach - 2024 - Ogegbo - Factors predicting teachers  implementation of inquiry‐based teaching practices  Analysis.pdf
metadata.title: Factors predicting teachers' implementation of inquiry‐based teaching practices: Analysis of South African TIMSS 2019 data from an ecological perspective
metadata.venue: Journal of Research in Science Teaching

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses TIMSS 2019 South Africa teacher and school contextual questionnaires merged with the TIMSS student achievement data via the IEA IDB Analyzer, and it analyzes Grade 9 science teachers nested in 520 schools. The authors state that sampling weights were used to select science teacher data and plausible science values, and that the teacher sampling weight was employed to construct most statistics. In the regression models, they explicitly fit the models with the sampling weight of science teachers, indicating complex survey design weighting was applied at the teacher level. The manuscript does not report replicate-weight methodology (e.g., BRR/jackknife), so uncertainty estimation is described only at the level of weighted regression rather than replicate-based variance estimation.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: Secondary analysis of TIMSS 2019 for South Africa using the nationally representative teacher and school contextual questionnaires. The analytic sample consists of Grade 9 science educators (teachers) from the TIMSS teacher contextual questionnaire, nested within 520 schools, and the study excludes TIMSS benchmarking participants. The authors also control for classroom achievement using the overall science proficiency score drawn from five plausible values, and they apply listwise deletion for missing data after testing missingness with Little’s MCAR; missing values were replaced with the mean while using listwise deletion to manage minimal missingness.

main_findings.dataset_used: TIMSS 2019 South Africa Grade 9 Science (Teacher Emphasize Science Investigation scale)
main_findings.target_variable: Inquiry teaching practice (ESI scale; teacher-reported frequency)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Hierarchical multiple regression (weighted). Final model (Step 5): R2 = 0.293, Adjusted R2 = 0.243, F(18,253) = 5.838, p < 0.001. Significant predictors in final adjusted model: Assessment strategy significance (β = 0.316, p < 0.001), Professional development (β = 0.152, p = 0.006), Resource shortage (β = 0.148, p = 0.015), Job satisfaction (β = 0.127, p = 0.037). Model step changes: Step 2 R2 = 0.074 (ΔR2 = 0.038, p = 0.027); Step 3 R2 = 0.254 (ΔR2 = 0.181, p < 0.001); Step 4 R2 = 0.284 (ΔR2 = 0.030, p = 0.015); Step 5 R2 = 0.293 (ΔR2 = 0.009, p = 0.0.?? not significant reported).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using TIMSS 2019 South Africa Grade 9 Science the study leveraged Assessment strategy significance, Inquiry-related professional development, Instructional resource shortage, and Job satisfaction to predict teachers’ inquiry teaching practice (ESI scale), finding that these mesosystem/exosystem factors were significant positive predictors in the final weighted hierarchical regression (final model R2 = 0.293; significant betas: 0.316, 0.152, 0.148, 0.127). This indicates that strengthening assessment practices aligned with inquiry and providing inquiry-focused professional development—alongside improving resource availability and teacher job satisfaction—may increase teachers’ reported implementation of inquiry-based teaching, though the study is correlational and based on self-reports rather than causal effects.

data.outcome_summary: This study uses TIMSS 2019 South Africa teacher contextual questionnaire data for Grade 9 science teachers (n = 537) to model teachers’ inquiry teaching practice using the Teachers Emphasize Science Investigation (ESI) scale. The outcome is teacher-reported frequency of inquiry activities (4-point Likert), and the analysis fits a weighted hierarchical multiple regression that controls for classroom science achievement using five plausible values. Across nested ecological layers (intrapersonal, microsystem, mesosystem, exosystem, macrosystem), the final model explains 29.3% of the variance in inquiry teaching practice (R2 = 0.293; F(18,253) = 5.838; p < 0.001). The strongest final predictors are teachers’ perceptions of the significance of assessment strategies (β = 0.316, p < 0.001), followed by inquiry-related professional development (β = 0.152, p = 0.006), instructional resource shortage (β = 0.148, p = 0.015), and job satisfaction (β = 0.127, p = 0.037). Limitations include non-experimental design (no causal inference) and reliance on self-reported perceptions rather than observed classroom inquiry quality.
